questions: The dossier's old card rests on canRelay's checkSig/ecrecover (RelayHub.sol:893-898, used via the recover at line 1520): canRelay is called from inside relayCall itself (RelayHub.sol:1566-1599), and on a bad signature the same call simply emits CanRelayFailed and returns (line ~1595-1599) without having paid or released anything yet. That is a signature checked in the same call that uses it, which patterns.md says is explicitly not PQ-15 ('a relayed call' is named as an excluded example). Does the registry agree this mechanism should be dropped as the basis for this card?

The only on-chain recheck in this contract that fits PQ-15's words (a signature already relied on, rechecked later to judge a past act) is penalizeRepeatedNonce/penalizeIllegalTransaction (RelayHub.sol:1789-1829): a relay signs two conflicting raw transactions off-chain (an act it cannot undo), and anyone can later submit them so the contract recovers the relay's address and slashes its stake, with no deadline in the code. If the relay (an EOA that only had to be an EOA at registration, RelayHub.sol:1411 'relay == tx.origin') moves to real code before being reported, both recoveries return no address under EIP-8151, addr1==addr2 trivially holds, and penalize(address(0)) then reverts at RelayHub.sol:1822-1824 ('Unstaked relay') since address(0) was never registered - so the fraud proof always fails and the relay keeps its whole stake. Is this read as a genuine PQ-15 finding, and if so is it MEDIUM (the relay's own stake is what goes unslashed; nobody else's funds are taken, the call simply reverts) or CRITICAL (an honest reporter who already holds the conflicting signatures is denied the reward)?

Whether any relay is currently staked, registered, or removed-but-not-yet-unstaked in this hub at block 26,438,999 (so a live reward/slashing path actually exists today) is a fact only RelayAdded/Staked/RelayRemoved/Unstaked event logs could show; the gateway refuses eth_getLogs ranges over 2,000 blocks, and the full history here runs from block 8,350,545. getRelay(address) on the two relay addresses seen in this address's last three transactions (0x7a6D8b5b5CF3773Cb518271e24aee626D9f6FF91, 0x0BE1241468df7E9D3b74a84869DDf05c36fD7E50) returns an all-zero entry, i.e. neither is currently staked; those two addresses' recent calls were withdraw/unstake, not relayCall or registerRelay, and the dossier's own trace shows canRelay-style recoveries (22,845 calls) stopping by block 24,504,093 with none recorded since. That stake()/registerRelay() remain open to anyone at any time (no admin gate, no expiry) means the path cannot be called closed for good even if no relay is staked today, but I cannot show whether one is staked right now without a wider log read than the gateway allows.
